correctness.rationale: Cyclotomic irreducibility forces equal rational aggregate coefficients. For a nonzero quadratic term, the exponent map has only (p+1)/2 values, so all aggregates vanish, exactly giving reflection-oddness. Two distinct reflections force a nonzero-translation invariance and hence the zero vector. The a=0 cases and full-support constants are separately proved. Sign counts use uniquely determined center and reflected pairs. Exhaustive exact-integer diagnostics p=5,7 and seeded p=11 samples agree; no finite data is substituted for the infinite-prime proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text inspection of Li’s arXiv:2609.16030v2 and Casazza–Fickus (2006), plus multi-alias published-finding corpus and web comparisons, found a genuine field-sensitive gap: Li proves sharp unrestricted-complex bounds but not the exact rational four-zero-set rigidity or sign enumerations. All identified close records were compared for logical implication, not title similarity. The familiar cyclotomic and quadratic-fiber ingredients are credited; unindexed antecedents remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Cyclotomic vanishing-sum and quadratic-folding arguments are classical and could appear as this precise combined rational-input theorem in older or unindexed literature not recovered in the searches.
Indexed finite-field Fourier results not returned by semantic search may contain equivalent sign-census formulas; no exhaustive priority certification is claimed.
The 2006 paper addresses pure chirps; the current result concerns rational linear combinations, and this distinction should be reassessed if a broader historical theorem is found.

value.rationale: This is an all-prime, all-support exact rigidity and counting theorem for rational quadratic Fourier signals, not a small numerical slice. It classifies every possible entire zero locus and gives closed sharp amplitude-constrained counts, showing a provably strict k-2 obstruction versus Li’s sharp complex optimum at every even support k>=4. That arithmetic gap is a natural invariant for one-bit chirp coding and finite mutually unbiased measurements and is not read off from the unrestricted complex bound.
